/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 24 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2882 (41)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4643 (91)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2131 (28)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1641 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 875 (1)
CAPESIZE
The market made a steady start to the week, with the Pacific maintaining a positive tone on healthy miner and operator activity, while the Atlantic was somewhat sluggish but continued to firm following stronger fixtures reported at the end of last week. The BCI 182 5TC increased by $817 to $42,105. In the Pacific, C5 was unchanged at $14.585, with two miners active. Offers began in the upper $14s, while bids were reported at $14.00 and $14.45. By the end of the day, fixtures were reported at $14.30 on more than one occasion, with another miner said to have paid around $14.50. The Atlantic was firmer, supported by stronger C3 fixtures reported last Friday. Activity was limited, however, with a noticeable lack of bids as the week got underway, offers were generally closer to $37 on C3, while the index increased by 0.400 to $36.182. Overall, the market began the week on a positive note, with the Pacific steady and well supported, while the Atlantic showed signs of improvement despite limited activity.
PANAMAX
A positive start to the week, after things appeared to turn at the end of last week, with all routes showing gains with the P5TC average up $250 to $19,178. The North Atlantic has seen a bounce from the floor of last week with increased offers, especially for early September positions out of US Gulf/US East Coast, whilst in the South it was a similar story for end September demand with rates showing a small improvement. In the Pacific it seemed a more subdued start, and although there was healthy NoPac grain demand, it appears to be matched by ample grain clean vessels. Limited Indonesian coal demand continues to mostly be covered on smaller/older types, but there still appeared to be a decent trickle of period fixing with the CSSC Yuan Jing (81,618 2018) Yokohama 5-6 September reportedly fixed for 2 years in the $18,000’s to Dai An. Western Bulk covered a grains stem NoPac/SE Asia for 15 September onwards, whilst Olam covered a 68,000/5 soyabeans stem NoPac/North China 1-15 Oct and Panocean were on subjects for a NoPac 12 September onwards requirement, but further details were lacking. The Orient U (79,754 2011) Van Phong 23-25 August was on subjects and the Ocean Dalian (75,599 2011) Mariveles 27-30 August fixed an Indonesian round voyage, but little else emerged.
SUPRAMAX
A rather subdued start as many collect and assess the market for the week ahead. The 11TC average was up $13 to $20,741, but there no significant movements in the individual routes.
The Van Hannah (63,926 2023) Chiwan 13-15 September was reported on subjects for one year with Fednav at $20,500 and Western Bulk took an Ultramax instead of a Panamax or Kamsarmax to cover their grains stem from West Australia to China 5th September onwards. The St-Cergue (60,696 2017) fixed basis passing Singapore for a trip via Indonesia to Bangladesh in the mid $26,000’s and the FW Venus (64,192 2023) prompt CJK fixed at around $21,000 for a trip via China to West Africa with steels/generals/vehicles etc. Oldendorff took the Jag Radha (58,133 2009) Fujairah prompt for inter Oman Gulf business at $24,000 and the Crimson Grace (61,133 2017) Chittagong 20-21 August fixed for an inter EC India coastal trade at $20,000, but the Charterer was unknown.
The African Isabelle (63,688 2022) Krishnapatnam 24 August agreed a trip via Indonesia redelivery India at about $20,000 whilst the Aquastar (61,225 2016) Krishnapatnam 18-19 August did a trip via EC India to China intention iron ore at $13,000 with Auxin.
HANDYSIZE
The week began in much the same vein as the previous one, with activity remaining subdued despite a slightly firmer undertone. Increased cargo availability in East Coast South America provided some encouragement, although participants largely remained on the sidelines as the market continued to assess conditions. As a result, there was little fresh activity reported.

The only notable piece of business emerged in the period market, where a 40,000 dwt vessel was reportedly fixed for one year at $17,000 per day.

Against this backdrop, the HS7TC edged higher, to close at $15,755, reflecting the modest improvement in sentiment despite the lack of fixture activity.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production

World crude steel output eased 0.4% from the same month last year to 149.2 Mt in July, World Steel Association data show. The drop came as Asian production fell 1.1% to 109.0 Mt, with a decline in China (-3.6% to 2.9 Mt) outweighing increased output in India (+1.9% to 14.4 Mt) and Vietnam (+34.7% to 2.7 Mt). Meanwhile, North American production rose 4.5% to 8.3 Mt, with European production increasing 4.2% to 14.2 Mt. In Jan-Jul, global crude steel output stood 0.7% lower than the same period last year at 1.1 Bt.

Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles

In the week to 21 August, Chinese iron ore stockpiles fell 0.6 Mt to 164.8 Mt, declining for the second consecutive week, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. However, inventories stood 26.9 Mt above the same time last year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was volatile today, closing marginally weaker after a firm start. September was the main focus, trading between 42,000–43,250. Early activity pushed up to 43,250 before the market came under pressure, with repeated trading around 42,250–42,500 and a move back towards 42,000 late in the day. Oct traded between 43,400–44,300, similarly easing from the morning highs to around 43,600–43,750 later on. The Sep v Oct spread widened and weakened today down to a low of -1500 early on, before recovering back up to -1400. Q4 26 was relatively steady around 42,000, trading between 41,850–42,150. Q1 27 traded between 28,550–28,650. Further out, Cal 27 traded between 32,200–32,450, while Cal 28 saw consistent activity at 28,250.

PMX
The PMX market was sold down through the session today. September was again the main focus, trading between 20,850–21,500. Early activity was concentrated around 21,250–21,500 before the market softened through the morning, with repeated prints around 20,900 and the contract closing near the lows at 20,850.
